text:
jen: heads up — acme-corp (acct: acct-9821) opened a billing dispute. They report streaming connections drop mid-response and our billing shows a 5xx and billed full token usage. Customer insists they closed client early, not a server error. they sent a minimal repro.

sana: linking the logs now. can you paste the exact request/headers + timeline? @mike FYI in case infra traces needed.

jen: pasted below (sanitized):

jen: ```
POST /v1/stream HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
Transfer-Encoding: chunked
Accept: text/event-stream

<client sends prompt>
...server streams tokens...
Client: FIN, RST after ~1.2s (capture shows FIN from client)
Server: logs show upstream write failed: broken pipe
```

jen: customer says our dashboard marks this as 5xx and billing invoices tokens as if server errored. they want refund for tokens after client closed.

mike: looking at gateway logs for that timeframe (2128600000). quick note: we currently map broken pipe / EPIPE in the edge to 5xx by default because upstream failed to finish streaming. that classification is what drives billing pipeline to include the request in "server error" bucket.

mike: i pulled envoy edge logs snippet:```
[envoy] 2026-08-21T14:00:02Z info stream id=12345 downstream connection closed: reason=connection termination
[app] 2026-08-21T14:00:02Z warn write failed: EPIPE
[billing] mark_request state=complete status=5xx tokens_charged=2048
```

sana: hmm — we need to decide if downstream-initiated FIN should be considered a client abort (4xx-ish) not a server 5xx. currently the heuristic is: if upstream write fails with EPIPE and response code unset -> classify 5xx. that was added years ago to catch server runtime panics that close sockets.

lela: from billing perspective, customers get refunded when we classify as client abort (we call it CLIENT_DISCONNECT) vs server error. ACME is requesting refund for tokens after client-close timestamp. their evidence is tcpdump showing client FIN at 14:00:02. Are we able to compute token cutoff reliably?

jen: customer also provided raw chunked frames — they show last chunk boundary at token 110, then client closed before server sent termination chunk. they were using a long streaming session.

sana: repro attempt: i ran a local curl with early client close:```bash
# stream then kill client quickly
curl -N -H "Transfer-Encoding: chunked" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d @prompt.txt https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream | head -n 1 &
sleep 0.8; kill $!
```

sana: observed server app logs: write to downstream failed: EPIPE. request lifecycle shows 'upstream finished sending' but downstream closed. billing job marks 5xx.

mike: so this is reproducible. options: 1) update gateway heuristics to check downstream T/F flags (i.e., if last event sent before EPIPE had normal data and connection close came from downstream, classify as CLIENT_ABORT) OR 2) patch billing pipeline to backfill refunds for specific dispute windows.

jen: customer wants immediate refund. can billing do an ad-hoc credit while eng plans a fix?

lela: yes, we can issue a one-off credit pending engineering verdict. please provide request_id(s) and times. For future we need an automated rule.

mike: engineering fix notes: the challenge is we can't always distinguish EPIPE caused by downstream vs EPIPE caused by upstream crash (process killed after partial write). but we have additional signals: runtime exit code, last trace span completion, and kernel-level TCP RST vs FIN. we can: 
- check process health around the time (if process alive -> likely client closed)
- examine envoy downstream connection logs (RST vs FIN)
- check if we emitted an internal 5xx span / exception

sana: i'd prefer a conservative change: only reclassify as CLIENT_ABORT when downstream FIN is observed before any internal exception spans and the app process remains healthy for 1s after the error. that avoids misclassifying real server crashes.

mike: agree. additionally we should capture token-offset of last flushed event to compute refundable token count. that requires instrumenting the write buffer to record last-flushed token index. low-risk: add metric 'stream.last_flushed_token' annotated with request_id.

jen: can you estimate ETA for small telemetry change + billing rule change? customer escalation needs update in 24h.

mike: telemetry change (emit metric) — ~1-2 days including rollout. heuristic change in gateway classification — ~2-3 days with canary. billing auto-refund rule: ~1 day.

lela: i'll issue immediate manual credit for acct-9821 once you confirm request ids. send me a short note for audit with reason "client-initiated disconnect dispute — manual credit".

jen: request ids: req=abcd-ef12-2128600000; timeline attached. please credit 1200 tokens.

eng-oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-5483 — streaming-client-close-billing-dispute. Owner: sana. Priority: P2.

sana: assigning self. immediate next steps: 1) mike will dump process health + envoy full connection trace for req abcd-ef12-2128600000 and paste here. 2) jen will coordinate refund with lela. 3) i'll open a PR with metric emission prototype and a short design doc for classification heuristic.

mike: dumps pasted:```
process pid=24321 alive=true uptime=27m
envoy downstream flags: FIN from client at 14:00:02.123 UTC
app traces: no unhandled exception spans; last flush event token_index=110 at 14:00:02.120
```

mike: given these signals, i think safe to classify as CLIENT_ABORT for this request.

lela: manual credit issued for acct-9821: credit id credit-2026-00077 amount=1200 tokens. audit logged.

jen: customer notified and happy for now. they asked about timeline for preventative fix.

sana: i'll draft the design doc and PR today. plan: emit 'stream.last_flushed_token' metric, add gateway heuristic to prefer CLIENT_ABORT if downstream FIN precedes EPIPE and no internal exception spans, and adjust billing aggregator to ignore token window after last_flushed_token when computing refunds. rollout: canary to 10% in 48h, full rollout 7 days after validation.

jen: thank you everyone. i'll close the support loop once GA credit and design doc links are in. :thumbsup:

mike: tagging for backlog: #infra-streaming-billing-heursitic

lela: closing note: if more disputes come in, escalate to finance@redwood with INC-2026-5483 ref.

jen: closing thread — will add final follow-up message when PR merges.
